# hs-sql-agent

> hs-sql-agent provides governed SQL access for AI agents through MCP, with fail-closed typed SQL compilation, scoped access policies, approval-gated DML, and support for PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Oracle, SQLite, and Firebird.

Current documented release: **2.0.3**. Product behavior is pinned to the immutable product tag `v2.0.3`.

The documentation site is localized in English, Traditional Chinese, Simplified Chinese, Japanese, Korean, French, and German. Prefer stable unversioned documentation URLs for the current release. Versioned Docs inherit unchanged pages from the immediate parent release and override only pages whose product behavior changed.

## Product consumption paths

- **Standalone service:** deploy the official Docker image / ToolBox composition.
- **Complete embedded product:** use `HsSqlAgent.Hosting` for the same standard first-party composition and configuration contract as Docker.
- **Custom ASP.NET Core integration:** use `HsSqlAgent.Server` when the host must own authentication, authorization, middleware, UI, telemetry, or approval-provider composition.

## Start here

- [Introduction](https://sql-agent.net/en/docs/getting-started/introduction): Security boundary, supported databases, and product consumption paths.
- [Quick start](https://sql-agent.net/en/docs/getting-started/quick-start): Docker, `HsSqlAgent.Hosting`, and `HsSqlAgent.Server` startup paths.
- [MCP client onboarding](https://sql-agent.net/en/docs/mcp/client-onboarding): Issue an MCP key and connect a client.
- [MCP tools reference](https://sql-agent.net/en/docs/mcp/tools-reference): The five built-in MCP tool contracts.

## Built-in MCP tools

The built-in surface remains intentionally small:

- `get_schemas`
- `get_tables`
- `get_columns`
- `execute_query_sql`
- `execute_dml_sql`

`execute_dml_sql` itself accepts one or more supported semicolon-separated DML statements. There is no separate `execute_dml_sql_batch` tool. A multi-statement request is approved once, executed in original order, and committed atomically inside one server-owned transaction. Client-supplied transaction-control SQL is rejected.

Published Custom Tools can extend a database's tool collection but are not additional built-in tools.

## SQL compiler and Safe DML

- [Execution model](https://sql-agent.net/en/docs/sql-compiler/execution-model): Parse, bind, authorize, validate, prove, compile, and execute.
- [SQL support](https://sql-agent.net/en/docs/sql-compiler/sql-support): Supported SQL surface and provider capability boundaries.
- [Database dialects](https://sql-agent.net/en/docs/sql-compiler/database-dialects): Provider-specific behavior for all six supported databases.
- [Safe DML](https://sql-agent.net/en/docs/sql-compiler/safe-dml): Atomic multi-statement approval, exact row-set evidence, revalidation, and rollback behavior.

For `UPDATE` and `DELETE`, approval binds exact primary-key row sets and each statement is revalidated immediately before mutation. `INSERT ... VALUES` binds immutable literal payloads and compiled commands. `INSERT ... SELECT` remains unavailable until source-rowset approval semantics are defined.

## DML approval providers

MCP Elicitation remains the default first-party approval provider. DML approval is transport-neutral and can also use the official `HsSqlAgent.Approvals.Webhook` adapter or a custom `IDmlApprovalProvider` in a modular host.

An asynchronous provider may return `Pending`. With Admin Store persistence, hs-sql-agent stores protected resume intent and approval fingerprints. Completion reloads current authorization and database configuration, reparses and previews the DML, compares evidence, and creates a fresh short-lived execution challenge. Approval systems never receive a database connection, transaction, validated execution plan, or commit primitive.

## ASP.NET Core integration

- [ASP.NET Core integration](https://sql-agent.net/en/docs/integration/aspnet-core): Standard Hosting versus modular Server composition.
- [ASP.NET Core product page](https://sql-agent.net/en/integrations/aspnet-core): Latest product positioning and representative configuration.

Use `HsSqlAgent.Hosting` for the batteries-included first-party composition. Use `HsSqlAgent.Server` when the application needs to replace or omit individual capabilities.

## Operations

- [Configuration](https://sql-agent.net/en/docs/operations/configuration): Docker environment, standard Hosting configuration, modular options, DML approval provider settings, telemetry, and distributed providers.
- [Deployment](https://sql-agent.net/en/docs/operations/deployment): Standalone, embedded, Webhook approval, persistence, and production guidance.
- [Distributed deployment](https://sql-agent.net/en/docs/operations/distributed-deployment): Shared Admin Store and Redis-backed coordination.
- [Observability](https://sql-agent.net/en/docs/operations/observability): Health, metrics, tracing, and operational visibility.
- [Upgrade guide](https://sql-agent.net/en/docs/reference/upgrade-guide): Release transition and rollback considerations.

The standalone / Docker environment includes these DML approval keys:

- `DML_APPROVAL_PROVIDER`
- `DML_APPROVAL_WEBHOOK_ENDPOINT`
- `DML_APPROVAL_WEBHOOK_CALLBACK_URL`
- `DML_APPROVAL_WEBHOOK_SIGNING_SECRET`

`DML_APPROVAL_PROVIDER` accepts `McpElicitation` or `Webhook`. The Webhook signing secret must contain at least 32 UTF-8 bytes.
